_comment: n8n → Settings → Variables. These are read by the workflow JSON in this folder as {{ $vars.NAME }}. The workflows are generated by build_workflows.py; this file is the other half of that contract.
_ladder_warning: The three agent tiers (Circle $44 / Pro $53 / Team $62) are the ONLY Whop products the entitlement code resolves. The one-time ladder below is a separate door and never grants agent access.

variables.description: Where the app lives. WF1/WF2 POST to $JARVIS_BRAIN_URL/api/brain; WF4 GETs /api/cron/daily-brief. No trailing slash.
Bearer token for /api/brain. Set the same value as N8N_BRAIN_TOKEN in Vercel. Generate: openssl rand -hex 32. Falls back to CRON_SECRET if unset.
Same value as CRON_SECRET in Vercel. Guards /api/cron/*.
Where WF1-WF5 report. Must match the Telegram credential.
Read-only mirror of lib/tiers.ts for message text. lib/tiers.ts is the source of truth; if these differ, tiers wins.
One-time ladder + the three agent tiers, in display order. One-times are $28 first shot / $17 Lite / $35 Good / $89 Better. Agent tiers $44/$53/$62.
GREEN < 50:1 ratio. Mirrors config/adaptable.json.
AMBER ceiling.
GREEN ER 5%+.
AMBER ER floor.
AMBER ER ceiling.
WF3 bar floor. PASS = replies >= max(25, ceil(views * 1%)).
Overridden per domain at generate time.
1 page = 1 YouTube brand (its own TikTok/IG/Shorts).
IG/TikTok/YouTube serious posts per day.
X discovery filler only, no gate, no DM.
CSV pool; WF1 ranks it down to the top five.
Vesper/Vapi number. Env only, not logged.
YouTube uses ManyChat.

Publishing goes through POST /api/publish, not to Buffer directly. The key and the five channel ids live in Vercel env, not here. WF5 never touches Buffer.

setup: n8n Cloud → Settings → Variables → Create each. Then import n8n/wf1_research.json … wf5_publish.json (or the bundle). Fill the two credential placeholders: Neon Postgres and the Telegram bot. Run WF4 first — it is the only one with no write side effects.
retired: The previous copy of this file said WHOP_LADDER_PRICES = $27+$9+$79+$19/mo. Those prices were retired; a workflow reading them would have advertised a $27 vault and a $19 Circle that no longer exist.
